candidate.title: repos[].path from the audited branch's config is not bounded to the project root before it is walked and bind-mounted
candidate.description: readProject accepts any non-empty repos[].path. The preflight and the sandbox runner resolve it with resolve(root, path), which allows absolute paths and '..' segments. The preflight walks the result, reads its manifests and, in a full audit, prints its top-level folders. The runner binds the same directory read-only into the container that runs target code. If the checked-out branch can change .agents/ultrapowers.json, which the architecture lists as audited-tree data, a branch author can point a repository outside the project and so give the hunt, and the sandbox that runs agent-chosen commands, a view of host files that are not part of the project. The image (digest-pinned, --pull=never) and the limits (validated) are bounded; the path is not.
candidate.claimed_root_cause: The config reader validates the repository name but not the path, so a value the audited tree can alter reaches the walk and the docker bind source as trusted input.

trace.description: repos[].path is read with text(r.path) from .agents/ultrapowers.json and kept as written; only emptiness is checked.
repoDir = resolve(root, repo.path) with no containment test; only existsSync is checked.
walk(repoDir), manifestsFromFiles and declaredFacts read the directory, and a full audit prints its top-level folders as tree: lines.
repoDir = resolve(root, entry.path) is bound read-only as /target (dockerArgs, line 130) into the container that runs the target's code (h2 owns the docker internals).

evidence.description: Control on the image: a digest pin, a local-cache check and --pull=never (line 128) bound the image; nothing equivalent exists for the path.
The scaffold writes nested relative repository paths, so a path outside the project is not part of the shipped layout.

blockers: Whether the audited branch's .agents/ultrapowers.json is the effective config of a hunt (a pull request branch checked out in the root) is a deployment fact outside source.
The sandbox is unavailable for this run, so no mount was observed.
Which host files a hunter or a container command could then read depends on the guardrail's read rules (h1) and the sandbox masks (h2), which are outside this unit.

validation_plan.local: In a dummy project, set a repos[].path to '..' or an absolute dummy folder, run hunt-preflight.mjs --full-audit and confirm the dummy folder is walked and its folders printed. In the sandbox, once available, confirm that dockerArgs binds that folder. Fix: refuse any path whose realpath is not inside the realpath of the project root, in readProject, so both consumers share the check.
validation_plan.deployment: The owner may confirm whether hunts are run on a pull request branch checked out in the project root, so that its config applies. If configs are always taken from the trusted base branch, this is hardening only.

checks.invariant: A repos[].path read from .agents/ultrapowers.json stays inside the project root before the preflight walks it, reads its manifests and hands it on as the repository folder
checks.result: readProject keeps text(r.path) as written and checks only that name and path are non-empty (hunt-files.mjs:59). loadProject validates only the ticket (hunt-preflight.mjs:518-537). preflight() then runs resolve(root, repo.path) (:564), which accepts an absolute path or '..' segments, and the result goes to walk(), declaredFacts() and (full mode) the SCOPE tree: lines. The path is checked for existence only (:565). The template ships only a relative nested path. Nothing in the three files bounds it. Sibling control: repo names are validated (:553, hunt-sandbox.mjs:263), paths are not.

checks.invariant: The sandbox's bind source, the sandbox image and the limits that come from the config are bounded before they reach docker run (h2 owns the docker argument internals; this check covers only the config-to-sink trust)
checks.result: Image: PINNED digest, --pull=never and a local-cache check in probe (:99-104) bound hunt.sandbox.images, so the audited config cannot select an arbitrary image. Limits: LIMIT_RULES validators (:68-70) bound hunt.sandbox.limits. Mount source: runCheck sets repoDir = resolve(root, entry.path) (:325) with no containment check and dockerArgs binds it read-only as source=<repoDir> (:130). A path outside the project would therefore be mounted into the container that runs target code, and the key-material masks are computed only inside that directory (maskPaths(repoDir), :115-121). This is the one config value reaching a sink as trusted input.
